paper.title_en: Easy-plane ferromagnetism in single-crystal ErB$_{2}$ at low temperatures
paper.abstract_en: We report a study of high-quality single crystals of the hexagonal rare-earth diboride ErB$_{2}$ prepared by means of the self-adjusted flux travelling-solvent floating-zone technique. Comprehensive measurements of the ac susceptibility, magnetization, specific heat, and electrical resistivity consistently establish a paramagnetic state at room temperature which develops strong easy-plane magnetic anisotropy of the hexagonal basal plane below a temperature $T_{\rm x} \approx 50$~K. Below a pronounced second-order phase transition at $T_{c} = 14$~K long-range magnetic order stabilizes. Excellent agreement with both the qualitative phenomenology and the quantitative characteristics of the thermodynamic and transport properties under applied magnetic fields up to 30\,T identifies the magnetic order in ErB$_2$ as a showcase par excellence of pronounced easy-plane ferromagnetism of Er$^{3+}$ local moments, in the presence of crystal electric fields and Van Vleck contributions.
